turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not threatened by you, Sandip. I am merely stating the facts, as I am bound to do by my duty as a zamindar.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in frivolous discussions with you, Sandip. I will have you removed from my estate, and I warn you, it will be done without any warning or appeal.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I see that the situation is growing more heated. Is there really a need for such strong words, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I think we should consider the implications of your words on our people. Your tenants and mine may be affected by any conflict.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's the point of removing me from your estate, Nikhil? I'm not a tenant, I'm the zamindar, after all.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so dramatic, never a fan of subtlety, are you? I'm shaking in my boots, or rather, in my jootis.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I think it would be wise to consider the interests of all parties involved, including your tenants and mine. Perhaps we could discuss this matter further in a more... tranquil atmosphere.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I must admit, Nikhil, your concern for the safety of our people is appreciated, but I do hope you're not suggesting that violence is the only solution to this problem.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, you're not suggesting that a few skirmishes between our tenants will bring the entire province to its knees, are you? I'm more concerned about your own property taxes being overdue.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Good heavens, Nikhil, are you actually trying to scare me into paying your debts by threatening me with a few rough-around-the-edges Mussulmans?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, perhaps we should focus on understanding the root causes of this tension, rather than simply addressing its symptoms.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your jests, Sandip. The threat is real, and I will not stand idly by while our people are put in harm's way.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you're so predictable. I'm not sure what's more laughable, the fact that you think I'm afraid of a few rowdy Mussulmans or that you actually think I'd pay you a rupee to avoid the trouble.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I've observed that both our tenants and the Mussulmans are struggling to make ends meet, Sandip. What efforts are you making to address their grievances?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, you're finally speaking sense, but it's a bit late, don't you think? Now Nikhil's got his feathers ruffled and he's convinced he's saving the day.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, do not underestimate the resolve of our Mussulman tenants. Their grievances are legitimate, and I will not stand by while you fan the flames of discord.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be responsible for the consequences of your actions, Sandip. The safety of our people is my top priority, and I will not be swayed by your indifference.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I implore you, Sandip, to consider the welfare of our tenants, rather than pursuing a path that may lead to bloodshed and destruction.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so dramatic, always so full of foreboding. What's next, a prophecy of doom and devastation? I'll believe the apocalypse is coming when I see it, not when you tell me it's imminent.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, I'm shaking in my boots, so full of fear and doubt. My tenants love me, I'm the benevolent zamindar, the one who keeps them in bread and circuses.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
